title: Tilt Glare Card
summary: A grid of four product cards where the card under the pointer leans toward it in 3D and a soft highlight slides across its face, settling back when the pointer leaves.
useWhen: product grid for a premium hardware or audio brand
small catalogue of collectible objects where each item deserves a moment
dark luxury storefront that needs depth without photography
portfolio cards that should feel like physical objects under a lamp
techniques: requestAnimationFrame loop that sleeps when settled

whyItWorks.how: The pointer only sets a target. A requestAnimationFrame loop moves rotation and glare 12 percent of the remaining distance each frame (--tilt-lerp: 0.12), so the card trails the cursor slightly and comes to rest instead of snapping. The loop stops once the summed error drops under 0.01, so idle cards cost nothing.

Tilt is capped at 8deg (--tilt-max) at the card edge and the lift is only 6px. Only the hovered card moves; its neighbours stay still, so the grid reads as one object picked up rather than four things wobbling.

Every :hover rule has a :focus-visible twin. A keyboard user gets the same 6px lift, the shadow and the glare parked at the top of the card, plus a brass inner ring. Tilt itself is gated to (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and to pointerType mouse, so touch never sees a card stuck at an angle.

The lift and shadow enter in 220ms and leave in 160ms with cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). People sweep across a product grid many times, so the response is short and the exit is about 25 percent faster than the entrance.

The loop writes four custom properties (--rx, --ry, --gx, --gy) on the hovered card only, and they feed transform and a gradient position. Nothing touches layout. The art and price sit at translateZ(26px) and translateZ(12px) inside preserve-3d, so the depth comes from the compositor.

directions.name: Playful
directions.change: Raise --tilt-max to 14deg, swap the dark surface for saturated flat colours per card, and replace the soft-light glare with a hard-edged diagonal sheen. Keep the lerp so the extra angle still settles.

directions.name: Editorial
directions.change: Drop the 3D tilt, keep only the glare and a 4px lift, and set product names in a large serif under each card. The highlight then reads as paper catching light rather than a device.

directions.name: Collectible
directions.change: Use a conic-gradient rainbow under the glare with mix-blend-mode color-dodge for a foil trading-card look, and raise --glare-opacity toward 0.8.

pitfalls: Setting overflow: hidden on the tilting element flattens preserve-3d, so the translateZ depth on the art disappears. Round the glare with border-radius: inherit instead of clipping.
Writing rotation straight from pointer coordinates makes the card twitch on every mouse jitter. Keep the target and the rendered value separate.
Leaving the tilt on for touch devices leaves the last-touched card frozen at an angle, because touch has no pointerleave in the usual sense.
Animating box-shadow on hover repaints a large blurred area every frame. Fade a pre-blurred pseudo-element's opacity instead.

tunables.name: --tilt-max
tunables.effect: Rotation at the card edge. Above 12deg the text starts to skew enough to hurt reading.

tunables.name: --tilt-lerp
tunables.effect: Fraction of the remaining distance covered per frame. Lower feels heavier, higher feels twitchy.

tunables.name: --perspective
tunables.effect: Camera distance. Smaller values exaggerate the near edge.

tunables.name: --glare-opacity
tunables.effect: Strength of the highlight on hover and focus.

tunables.name: --lift
tunables.effect: Vertical lift on hover and keyboard focus.

reducedMotion: Tilt and lift are removed. Hover and focus still fade in the shadow and a fixed glare near the top of the card over 220ms, and focus keeps the brass ring, so the state change stays visible without any movement.
